headline: GitHub has made remote control for its Copilot coding assistant generally available, so a developer can start a session on a computer and finish it from a phone.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a real product release for people who code with Copilot, but the only report found is a few sentences with no detail.
importance_line: Developers who use Copilot can keep an AI coding task going away from their desk, though the report gives no detail on limits, price or which plans include it.
summary: TechGig reports that remote control for GitHub Copilot, GitHub's AI coding assistant, is now generally available, meaning open for general use rather than limited testing. The article says developers can start work in the VS Code editor or the command line and finish it from their phone, through github.com or the GitHub Mobile app.
notes: The TechGig page is a very short item (a few sentences), read in full; GitHub's own announcement and a second outlet were not found. Event date not stated.
